sections.title: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
sections.abstract: The authors construct a planar counterexample to eigenvalue-only criteria for sub-Gaussian heat-kernel bounds, then give a characterization using first Dirichlet eigenpairs under geometric and analytic hypotheses.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that the bottom Dirichlet eigenvalue on balls alone does not characterize the heat-kernel upper bound, and prove an equivalence using the first eigenvalue together with a uniform comparison of the first eigenfunction's supremum and its value at the ball center.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The main equivalence is for unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet spaces with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling, and a scale-r^β Poincaré inequality; an additional exit-time/spectral equivalence is stated under an elliptic Harnack inequality.
sections.unique_caveat: The planar counterexample warns against dropping exit-time controls; the positive characterization is conditional on the stated space and regularity assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.75, entirely from three cross-lists; placed first for combining a concrete counterexample with a corrected spectral characterization and a stated resolution of a prior conjecture.

sections.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
sections.abstract: In a four-dimensional Hamiltonian reduction of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system, the author shows that a transverse intersection of invariant manifolds near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet yields infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits.
sections.claimed_result: Given a transverse intersection away from the bouquet (a super-homoclinic orbit), the author proves the existence of infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits, corresponding to multi-bump localized standing waves.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The saddle eigenvalues satisfy 0 < λ1 < λ2 < 2λ1, with further nondegeneracy assumptions; the conclusion is conditional on the transverse intersection of the constructed invariant manifolds.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not establish that the required transverse intersection occurs for a particular parameter regime of the coupled system.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.75, entirely from three cross-lists; the placement reflects the explicit conditional multiplicity theorem linking Hamiltonian dynamics to localized wave states.

sections.title: Breaking Resonance: Square-root acceleration for Metropolis-adjusted randomized Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
sections.abstract: For randomized integration-time laws satisfying a Fourier non-resonance condition, the author proves a warm-start mixing bound for Metropolis-adjusted HMC with velocity Verlet and gives a lower-bound example when Hessian regularity is removed.
sections.claimed_result: For an m-strongly convex potential with L-Lipschitz gradient and L_H-Lipschitz Hessian, expected gradient evaluations to reach fixed total-variation accuracy are, up to constants and logarithmic factors, of order sqrt(κd) + sqrt(L_H)(d/m)^(3/4), with κ=L/m. The paper also gives a κ^(2/3)-scale obstruction, up to logarithms, when Hessian regularity is absent.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The upper bound assumes a warm start, fixed step-size Verlet integration, the stated strong-convexity/smoothness conditions, and a non-resonant duration law; uniform, exponential, and triangular laws are given as examples.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly do not establish optimality of the upper bound's L_H dependence; Hessian regularity matters for fixed-step performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.50, entirely from two cross-lists; ranked highly for a quantified mixing result, a matching cautionary lower bound, and a linked Lean 4 formalization of the main results.

sections.title: Monadicity of noncommutative measurable spaces over C*-algebras
sections.abstract: The authors establish a monadic description of σ-C*-algebras over C*-algebras and derive universal descriptions of probabilistic morphisms, local presentability, a tensor product, and a formulation of CP-instruments.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the forgetful functor from σ-C*-algebras with σ-normal *-homomorphisms to C*-algebras is monadic, and use this framework to characterize σ-cpu maps, construct a tensor product, and obtain a correspondence for σ-CP-instruments.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The results concern monotone σ-complete C*-algebras and σ-normal morphisms; the paper builds on the authors' proposed noncommutative analogue of measurable spaces.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that the resulting symmetric monoidal category is not closed; the framework is a proposed analogue, not an equivalence with ordinary measurable spaces in full generality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.50, entirely from two cross-lists; ranked for a structural theorem that connects category theory and operator algebras and supports several explicitly stated consequences.

sections.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
sections.abstract: For a linear symbolic matrix whose nonconstant coefficient matrices have rank at most r, the author proves that every blow-up size k ≥ r attains its noncommutative rank and derives algorithmic and polyhedral consequences.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that blow-up size k ≥ r suffices when the nonconstant coefficient matrices have rank at most r, and gives a randomized nc-rank algorithm for fixed r plus stabilization of a related polytope hierarchy at level r.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The matrices may be rectangular over an arbitrary field; the coefficient A0 is unrestricted, while each other coefficient has rank at most r. The stated arithmetic-operation bound assumes a sufficiently large field and constant r.
sections.unique_caveat: The algorithmic consequence is restricted to fixed coefficient-rank bound and sufficiently large fields; the theorem does not claim an analogous fixed-size bound without the low-rank hypothesis.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.50, entirely from two cross-lists; the placement reflects a precise rank-bounded stabilization theorem with computational and polyhedral applications.

sections.title: Gaps between zeros of Epstein zeta-functions of binary quadratic forms on the critical line
sections.abstract: For integral binary quadratic forms with nonsquare discriminant up to sign, the authors prove that the associated Epstein zeta-function has a critical-line zero within T^(2/5+ε) of every sufficiently large height T, improving prior exponents in several cases.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish a T^(2/5+ε) proximity bound for all sufficiently large T; for discriminant −4m² with m odd they obtain exponent 1/3. Their method includes an additive-twist Voronoi formula and two-dimensional Weyl differencing.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Q is an integral binary quadratic form whose discriminant, up to sign, is not a perfect square; the bound is for zeros on the critical line and for all sufficiently large T.
sections.unique_caveat: The exponents retain an arbitrary ε-loss, and the result does not assert a uniform exponent of 1/3 for every eligible discriminant.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.00; selected as a notable result for an explicit improvement below the classical 1/2 exponent for indefinite forms and an especially strong 1/3 exponent in the stated negative-discriminant case.

sections.title: The optimal exponent in the Babai-Goodman-Pyber theorem
sections.abstract: For a finite group X and soluble subgroup H, the author identifies the least exponent bounding [X:Rad(X)] by a power of [X:H], and proves sharpness of the associated coefficient in the nonsoluble case.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that the least possible exponent is b₀ = 1 + log₉(168·24^(1/3)) ≈ 3.8141 and that the coefficient 24^(−1/3) in the stronger nonsoluble-group inequality is optimal.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: X is finite and H is a soluble subgroup; Rad(X) is the largest soluble normal subgroup. The proof reduces to bounds on soluble subgroups of automorphism groups of finite simple groups.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is confined to finite groups and soluble subgroups; sharpness is demonstrated by examples based on PSL₂(8), not by a classification of all equality cases.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.00; selected as a notable result because it determines the exact optimal exponent and gives examples establishing sharpness, rather than for a measured attention signal.

sections.title: An improved estimate for discrete L^8 restriction on the cubic curve
sections.abstract: The authors prove a discrete eighth-moment restriction estimate for the cubic curve (n,n³), saving a factor N^(1/47500) over the N^(1/2+ε) scale.
sections.claimed_result: For every ε>0, the paper bounds the eighth moment of Σ_{n≤N} b_n exp(2πi(nx+n³y)) over [0,1]² by a constant depending on ε times N^(1/2−1/47500+ε)(Σ|b_n|²)^4.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The estimate is for the stated cubic frequency set, arbitrary coefficients bₙ, and every ε>0; the implied constant may depend on ε.
sections.unique_caveat: The power saving 1/47500 is small, and the abstract does not claim that the exponent is optimal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.00; included as a concrete harmonic-analysis bound improvement, with its displayed power saving providing a checkable mathematical basis for selection.
